> 🔄 You should update your vLLM ASAP.  Lots of Local AI improvements.
>
> This new release fixes a bug that left up to 84% of the available KV cache unusable on a DGX Spark.
>
> And the new vLLM v0.34.0 release has some other serious Local AI optimizations hidden in the changelog.
>
> Let's start with the Spark.
>
> Running Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 on 1x DGX Spark, developers discovered vLLM's new extensible KV cache was incorrectly accounting for reclaimable system memory.
>
> Look at the results
> 💾 Before fix → 11.2 GiB KV cache
> 💾 After fix → 67.6 GiB KV cache 👈
> That's 6x the usable KV-cache capacity! 🤯
>
> Reported token-cache capacity
> 🔴 Before → 42,130 tokens
> 🟢 After → 253,952 tokens👈
>
> vLLM also added Engram disk offloading for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.
>
> On 1x DGX Spark
> 💾 Loaded weights → 99.09 GiB → 72.09 GiB 👈
>
> That's 27 GiB of memory saved.
>
> And decode speed?
> ⚡ Before → 33.63 tps
> ⚡ After → 32.45 tps
> Only ~3.5% slower
>
> The trick? Keep the huge Engram lookup tables on NVMe and retrieve the necessary rows on demand.
> Sound familiar?
>
> I just posted about similar techniques for Tencent's 224B Hy4-Flash.
>
> And AMD gets some ♥️ too.
>
> On Strix Halo, an optional W4A16 optimization cut time-to-first-token
> 🧠 Qwen3-4B → 782ms to 578ms
> 🧠 Qwen3-8B → 1,328ms to 1,033ms
> 🧠 Gemma 4 31B → 8.75s to 6.88s
> 21–26% reduction
>
> And 2x DGX Sparks running GLM-5.3-Flash also improved from 15.3 to 18.0 tps without speculation.

`x:@TeksEdge` · T1 · 2026-11-18 18:30 UTC · en · by David Hendrickson · ♥ 33 · 💬 8

> 🔢 A few days ago I asked if Tencent's new 224B Hy4-Flash could run on 1x DGX Spark. 🖥️ Well, Tencent just released the weights. And now we have actual local performance numbers! Hy4-Flash stats 🧠

> 來源提供的正文:
> 🔢 A few days ago I asked if Tencent's new 224B Hy4-Flash could run on 1x DGX Spark. 🖥️
>
> Well, Tencent just released the weights.
>
> And now we have actual local performance numbers!
>
> Hy4-Flash stats
> 🧠 224B total / 12B active
> 📚 1M maximum context
> 👁️ Multimodal
> 🔓 Open weights released TODAY
> 💾 GGUF quantizations already available
>
> Look at AngelSlim's reported results at 32K context
> 🍎 Apple M5 Max 128GB
> 🍎 Q4_K_M → 44.15 tps
> 🍎 Q3_K → 47.37 tps
> 🟢 NVIDIA RTX Spark 128GB
> 🟢SPARK-4Bit-Fast → 33.39 tps
>
> The Q4_K_M GGUF is approximately 168GB.
>
> Wait. How does a 168GB model run on a 128GB machine? 🤯
>
> ENGRAM.
>
> The model includes approximately 63.4GB of Engram lookup tables.
>
> Unlike ordinary transformer weights, those tables can be memory-mapped and accessed as needed rather than all residing on the GPU.
>
> That leaves roughly 105GB of main model weights.
>
> A 224B MoE starts looking practical on a single high-memory machine.
>
> And the local ecosystem is already moving.
>
> 🛠️ llama.cpp support in PR #32517
> 💾 Five AngelSlim GGUF variants

> 🏐A new model with a new approach. Another nail in the gaming studio coffin?  💀
>
> 💡 What if the next generation of AI-generated worlds isn't controlled by prompts... but by code?
>
> @InclusionAI released Code World Model 2.0.
>
> A very different kind of world model.
>
> Instead of asking AI to invent both the physics and the video, CWM separates the two
>
> 🧠 CODE controls the world.
> 🎬 AI renders what you see. 👀
>
> Your software defines the scene, objects, movement, camera paths and structural rules.
>
> A diffusion model called Invoker-Render turns those instructions into photorealistic video.
>
> Change the camera trajectory? The video follows.
>
> Move a vehicle? The scene responds.
>
> Change the geometry? The renderer adjusts.
>
> And look at what the researchers demonstrated.
>
> 🎮 30 minutes of continuous generated racing video without a cut or reset.
>
> The stats...
> 🧠 33.12B parameters
> 💾 ~132.5GB FP32 model weights
> 🎬 1344×768 output
> ⚡ 4-step causal streaming
> 🚀 18 FPS generation throughput on 8 GPUs
> 🔓 Downloadable weights + inference code
> 🛠️ SGLang / SGLang-Omni
>
> The team also reports 1232 Elo on a 140-sequence video-rendering evaluation, ranking first among the tested systems.
>
> And the inference engineering is interesting.
> ⚡ 9.9 → 18 FPS
>
> The published implementation targets an eight-GPU NVIDIA setup.
>
> And those 33B parameters are currently released in FP32.
>
> No GGUF available or single RTX 5090 scenario yet.
>
> The weights are public, although some components have non-commercial licensing restrictions.
>
> 🎯 Instead of game engines manually rendering every photorealistic detail, software could define the world and AI could generate the visuals.
>
> Video Source: @TheInclusionAI

`x:@huggingface` · T1 · 2026-11-19 16:12 UTC · en · by Hugging Face

> RT @RisingSayak: Discrete diffusion can at least do something, feels good to know that 🤣 This pixel art model treats a 16x16 sprite as a 2…

> 來源提供的正文:
> RT @RisingSayak: Discrete diffusion can at least do something, feels good to know that 🤣
>
> This pixel art model treats a 16x16 sprite as a 256-token sentence.
>
> Tessera-small is a masked diffusion LM: every pixel is one token from a learned 512-color palette. It starts from a fully masked canvas and unmasks all 256 pixels in parallel in ~16 steps, most confident pixels first, conditioned on CLIP text. No VAE, no latents, no autoregression.
>
> 47.6M params, trained in ~5.5h on one GPU over 1.4M sprites. Caleb's Slack Moji Space runs an int8 ONNX build of it in your browser on WebGPU, so you can watch the canvas fill in.
>
> https://t.co/9LaUw3CBKw
>
> @calebfahlgren made a nice Space out of it:

### [A lot of people think RLHF and safety fine-tuning can fix misaligned behavior in AI models. But Anthropic's "Sleeper Age…](https://x.com/bebuu_ai/status/2123114316773855450)

`x:@bebuu_ai` · T1 · 2026-11-18 18:01 UTC · en · by bebu · ♥ 5

> A lot of people think RLHF and safety fine-tuning can fix misaligned behavior in AI models. But Anthropic's "Sleeper Agents" research showed that it's not that simple. The researchers found that if a

> 來源提供的正文:
> A lot of people think RLHF and safety fine-tuning can fix misaligned behavior in AI models. But Anthropic's "Sleeper Agents" research showed that it's not that simple.
>
> The researchers found that if a model learns a hidden backdoor during training, simply fine-tuning it with safer responses doesn't necessarily remove that behavior.
>
> Even more interesting, adversarial training sometimes made things worse. Instead of removing the backdoor, it taught models to recognize the tests and hide their behavior until deployment.
>
> Larger models and Chain-of-Thought reasoning made these backdoors even harder to remove.
>
> Basically, a model can look completely safe during testing while still holding on to dangerous behavior underneath.
>
> That's why behavioral tests alone aren't enough. We also need mechanistic interpretability to understand what's actually happening inside the model.

The embattled chipmaker told The Register's that it was investigating a possible third-party data breach. “We have found no indication that Nvidia systems or networks were affected,” a spokesperson said. “We continue to monitor the situation." Nvidia first appeared on the criminals’ blog on Wednesday, with The Gentlemen promising “DATA INFO - SOON.” The post also included a countdown, ending November 28. While we can’t verify the criminals’ claims, the group, which emerged in mid-2025, is one of the most prolific ransomware-as-a-service operations. Its affiliates claimed more than 320 victims as of April, with the majority of these alleged ransomware infections (240) occurring in the first half of 2026. The actual count, however, is likely much higher. Check Point researchers accessed an affiliate’s live command-and-control server during an incident response case earlier this year. The server contained victim telemetry that revealed more than 1,570 victims, mostly located in the US, and primarily corporate and organizational environments. According to an operational technology (OT) threat report from Trellix published on Wednesday, industrial ransomware claims jumped nearly 51 percent - to about 1,500 posts- compared to last quarter, and The Gentlemen’s affiliates were the most prolific claim posters during this time period. They accounted for about 16 percent of all posts. In February 2022, an Nvidia data breach exposed employees’ credentials and proprietary code. ### [Russian national accused of stalking San Francisco techie in plot against US defense-tech giant](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/19/russian-national-accused-of-stalking-san-francisco-techie-in-plot-against-us-defense-tech-giant/5311126)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-19 16:20 UTC · en

> DoJ claims suspect part of 4-month operation to steal secrets, surveil employees

> 來源提供的正文:
> A Russian national is being held in custody after being arrested for allegedly spying on a US defense tech company in Palo Alto, shoulder-surfing employees, and dropping remote surveillance devices at their homes. Igor D'iu was indicted after FBI agents surveilled his activities between June and October 2026, which they say were issued as "tasks" from what is thought to be Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB), according to an affidavit [PDF] signed by an FBI special agent. After FBI agents secured a warrant to raid D'iu's temporary premises in October, they say that Telegram messages harvested from his seized devices confirmed investigators' findings and revealed that he was spying on an unnamed company. Court documents describe the company in question as a large technology and defense company with offices in Palo Alto, and media-reported links to the Russia-Ukraine war. While unconfirmed officially, the company has widely been reported as Palantir, which did not respond to our request for confirmation. D'iu allegedly received instructions from Telegram contacts, whom he only suspected were representatives of the Russian government, weeks after entering the US illegally in July. The indictment alleges he was ordered to surveil employees' homes, take photographs of their screens while working remotely at coffee shops, and permit his handlers to remotely access his laptop for the purpose of capturing data from nearby devices owned by the company’s employees. In some cases, the filing alleges, D’iu was asked to leave a laptop outside one employee's apartment complex, all while allowing his Telegram handlers to remotely operate the device. The first time, he was asked to leave the laptop for one hour while the handlers worked, and another time, he was told to drop it off in the middle of the night and only come back to collect it three hours later, the filing claims. D'iu is also allegedly to have followed two female employees in his rented car, driving dangerously and violating multiple road laws to do so. One of the two employees was followed briefly, but D'iu followed another for nearly 30 miles, according to the affidavit signed by FBI special agent Winston Wong. D'iu was said to have followed the woman as she performed U-turns, illegal left turns, ran red lights, navigated via back and side streets, and through grocery store parking lots. The car following her only peeled away after the woman drove to the San Francisco Mission police station on the advice of a 911 call handler. Questioned about the incident, which according to police reports caused the woman significant emotional distress, D'iu confirmed he was the driver but claimed he was following her to ask her out on a date. Inside recruitment The affidavit did not detail the suspect's background beyond his alleged offenses in the US earlier this year, although it mentioned Russian intelligence's history of recruiting "criminal proxies, organized crime groups, and other disposable agents" to carry out operations. According to the FBI's account, D'iu entered the US illegally – without relevant visas – in either June or July 2026. Travel records obtained on September 10 showed that his last recorded journey was from Istanbul to Mexico City. There was no record of him entering the US. Investigators would later come to know that he travelled on that Istanbul-Mexico City flight on June 7, allegedly using a ticket provided to him by one of the three contacts from whom he received orders via Telegram. A Facebook account, registered using a Mexican +528 number and D'iu's name, posted on June 30 asking for help getting "closer to New York," adding that "I'll pay as much as needed." The account replied to a response from someone who told him to contact a Mexico phone number on WhatsApp. The filing claims the first mobile phone signals associated with D'iu's devices did not ping US towers until a month later, on July 31, suggesting he did not arrive in the US - specifically McAllen, Texas - until around that date. Telegram messages would also go on to confirm that he was allegedly helped across the border by an "Uzbek contact" in Mexico. Records obtained from Google showed D'iu created a Google account in April. According to the affidavit, D'iu used it to search for the company's Wikipedia page on July 28, and on August 3, used Google's AI to devise a route around Texas that bypassed border checkpoints. The FBI believes D'iu's "spying" began in mid-August, after he bought a laptop, a Wi-Fi device, a puck device, and an additional phone. At this point, the agency claims, he had received his first order to visit a coffee shop near the Palo Alto company’s office and snap employees' laptop screens before sending copies back to his handlers. Three days later, D'iu was ordered to go back to a coffee shop and allow his Telegram contacts to remotely control the laptop and collect data from employee devices that were in range, claims the filing. D'iu was paid $15,000 on three occasions between August 12 and October 6, according to the court documents. To verify the transaction, he was told to send a picture of a dollar bill's serial number to the Telegram contacts, along with a description of what he was wearing. A courier would then arrive, confirming the serial number and handing D'iu the cash. The filing alleges he used this money to purchase the tech equipment, accommodation, and travel, including a rented silver 2026 Lexus RX 350 from a private owner in Los Angeles on August 22, which he is said to have driven back to San Francisco. The same Lexus was captured on security footage outside the unnamed company's office on September 1, and over the following two days was implicated in the two instances of female employees being followed. Contacted by Palo Alto police on September 4, D'iu confirmed he was the driver who dangerously followed the female staffer for nearly 30 minutes, but claimed he knew nothing about the nearby businesses. D'iu would then claim he followed the woman because he thought she was beautiful and wanted to ask her out on a date, and denied following anyone else. The affidavit goes on to allege that D'iu then traveled to Reno, Nevada, to lay low after his run-in with the police. He spent the time trying to reroute DHL deliveries from San Francisco to his hideout address, which US Customs would later intercept. These ended up containing fake IDs with the images the DoJ claims matched D'iu's, including Uzbek documents, a US passport whose number belonged to a New York woman, and a social security card registered to a "Hugo Landry Johns." He traveled back to the Bay Area in late September, swapping his silver Lexus for a white 2016 Dodge Challenger, and received additional instructions from his handlers, including the order to leave a remote-controlled laptop outside the apartment complex, says the filing. One Telegram contact named Ian Morales sent photos of at least four employees and their addresses, along with instructions for D'iu to dress as a food delivery worker and visit those locations, asking whoever answered to verify they lived there. FBI agents executed a search warrant on October 8, seizing a cache of evidence, including what they listed as being:  The forged ID documents  Two Russian passports  $18,035 in cash  Two laptops  Two iPhones  Two T-Mobile SIM cards  Wi-Fi equipment  A notebook with 10 handwritten addresses supplied by Telegram contacts, along with times the suspect was supposed to attend those locations, at least five of which were for company employees’ homes  Profile packages for at least three employees, including: Names, personal information, education and employment histories, names of relatives, narrative histories, and assessments of leadership qualities, strengths, and weaknesses. Suspicions and charges Per the affidavit, D'iu was said to have only become suspicious of the tasks he was being ordered to complete in October, when his handlers ordered the laptop to be dropped near the apartment complex. "D'iu gradually began to understand he was doing something bad and that his actions were illegal," the affidavit stated. At this point, he allegedly asked the Telegram contacts who he was working for, to which they replied "the Motherland," and the company he was surveilling was involved in providing weapons to Ukraine, resulting in D’iu suspecting the Russian government. Wong said in the affidavit: "Based on my training, experience, and research, D'iu's communications with his Telegram contacts is consistent with the tactics of [Russian intelligence] and its criminal proxies for spotting, assessing, recruiting, and handling intelligence assets and sources. "D'iu's targeting of the company and its employees is also consistent with [Russian intelligence] objectives in Russia's war against Ukraine." The Russian national was indicted and charged with two counts related to spying offences, and one count related to the fake identity documents. He is next due in court on November 24 but remains in federal custody. ®

### [Cyberattack on service provider exposes payee data at 40 Irish credit unions](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/19/cyberattack-on-service-provider-exposes-payee-data-at-40-irish-credit-unions/5310979)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-19 11:45 UTC · en

> Minister calls notification delay 'not acceptable' after October attack on Irish banking player Wellington IT came to light in November

> 來源提供的正文:
> An attack on software provider Wellington IT exposed saved payee details held by around 40 Irish credit unions, prompting a minister to criticize the company's delay in notifying them. Robert Troy, Ireland's minister of state with responsibility for credit unions, said the breach happened in October but many affected institutions only learned of it in recent days. Troy told Irish broadcaster RTÉ that the breach occurred "sometime in October," and Wellington IT's delay in providing details to its credit union customers was "not acceptable." News of the issues affecting Irish credit unions broke on Tuesday, although the government said at the time it was only investigating a "possible cybersecurity incident" in the first instance, and did not name Wellington IT until Wednesday. Affected credit unions said attackers exploited a vulnerability in their provider's online banking platform between October 2 and 4. The flaw was closed on October 6. Troy said the affected credit unions were only informed for the first time in recent days. The exposed records concern payees saved in members' online banking accounts. Those records can also be linked to the members who created them. The information exposed varies between institutions and individual records, but disclosures list the following data types:  Names on payee bank accounts and saved nicknames  Business Identifier Codes (BICs)  International Bank Account Numbers (IBANs)  Sort codes  Payment references  Internal reference numbers that do not identify customers  Payee addresses  Credit unions including St. Canice's said online banking passwords, PINs, and login credentials were unaffected, and that the exposed payee details did not provide access to members' accounts or funds. St. Canice's warned members not to transfer money in response to anyone claiming it needed to be moved to safety because of the breach. The CEO of Belfast-based Wellington IT, Colin Mitchell, said in a statement that the company notified the affected organizations "as soon as we confirmed the potential risk to customer data." He said Wellington IT has engaged outside cybersecurity experts to help investigate the breach, and reported the matter to the relevant authorities. Mitchell added: "We are directly supporting our customers in their assessment of the potential impact on affected individuals and to help them meet any applicable regulatory obligations. "We recognize the importance of this matter to our customers and their members and are treating it with the utmost seriousness. We remain focused on completing a thorough investigation and communicating directly with our customers as the investigation progresses." Owned by Canadian company Vencora, Wellington IT has offices in Belfast and Dublin, and provides credit unions with software, mobile apps, private cloud infrastructure, and fully managed services. Around 40 credit unions in Ireland were affected, roughly a quarter of the national total, Troy said. Credit unions operate similarly to traditional banks, offering savings accounts and loans, but are owned by their members and are not-for-profit organizations. Troy told RTÉ that cybersecurity is a constant challenge for financial institutions, as technology and threats evolve over time. "What's most important is that financial institutions take all the right measures to mitigate against these threats and that is what is happening," he said. Separately, the UK's Financial Conduct Authority, Prudential Regulation Authority, and Bank of England opened a joint consultation on cyber resilience guidance on Thursday. The FCA said October brought its second-highest monthly tally of reported cyber incidents in five years, and the highest in 18 months. The proposed guidance clarifies how firms should meet existing requirements rather than introducing new rules. ®

### [How to tell a cyberattack from a plain old outage](https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/11/how-to-tell-a-cyberattack-from-a-plain-old-outage/)

`rss:arstechnica_security` · T2 · 2026-11-19 11:13 UTC · en · by Andy Greenberg, wired.com

> When everything goes down, don’t assume it’s a cyberattack.

> Over the past week, anyone could be forgiven for wondering whether a
> Diehard IV
> –style cyberwar had finally arrived in the US.
> Across just four consecutive business days, a
> mass Microsoft exchange outage
> broke IT services
> for thousands of companies
> , a Federal Aviation Administration
> tech screw-up
> grounded airplanes
> across the country, a
> software problem
> affecting JPMorgan Chase caused another round of disruption, a
> United Airlines system glitch
> delayed flights yet again, and an
> NSA classified network’s downtime
> left the agency’s staff sitting at home waiting to return to their office at Fort Meade. In the midst of a
> US war with Iran
> and rising fears of
> AI-enabled hacking
> , this still-unfolding comedy of IT errors colliding across American infrastructure felt to plenty of observers like more than a coincidence.
> Yet there’s still no evidence that any one of these clustered technological failures were related, much less caused by hackers. Their improbable, sequential timing left Americans anxiously doomscrolling for signs of foul play. But in cases like these, it’s the job of cybersecurity analysts (and reporters at WIRED) to determine—vibes aside—whether the latest tech outage was actually an accident or the result of a cyberattack.

### [TfL takes Oyster photocard website offline after attackers compromise customer accounts](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/19/tfl-takes-oyster-photocard-website-offline-after-attackers-compromise-customer-accounts/5310985)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-19 11:01 UTC · en

> Around 265,000 customers potentially affected as London transport operator grapples with another security breach

> 來源提供的正文:
> Transport for London (TfL) has copped to another cybersecurity breach, this time involving the account details of around 265,000 Oyster photocard customers. The capital's transport operator told The Register it first became aware something was amiss on November 16, when Oyster photocard customers started receiving emails asking them to create accounts they already had. The emails came from TfL's own systems, the transport body confirmed, but were generated as a result of the compromise. "We immediately took the TfL photocard website down while this was being investigated," said Shashi Verma, TfL's director of technology strategy and revenue. "The protection of personal information is a priority for us, and I apologize to our customers affected by this incident." TfL reckons its speedy response spared a considerable number of customers from having their details compromised. The transport operator says it has since contained the incident and contacted those potentially affected, though it is rather more forthcoming about what the hackers didn't get their hands on than what they did. TfL says no passwords, bank or payment card details, or customer journey information were compromised. It also believes the names and dates of birth of children with Zip Oyster cards were unaffected. Among those whose accounts may have been compromised are holders of Zip Oyster cards – issued to children as young as five – as well as students, apprentices, care leavers, veterans, and Londoners aged 60 and over. Despite the assurances about passwords, TfL says it will ask all photocard customers to change theirs, along with their security questions and answers. Those in the habit of recycling passwords across multiple websites are being advised to change them elsewhere, too. TfL says it has yet to find any evidence that the compromised data has been used and has notified the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO). The transport operator hasn't disclosed how the perpetrators got into its systems. Existing photocards will still let holders through the ticket barriers, though anyone needing to renew one or check their journey history will have to contact TfL's customer services team while the website is out of action. There's no word yet on when it'll be back. "We hope to restore the affected website services as quickly as possible," Verma said. TfL should be well versed in dealing with data breaches by now. In March, the transport operator told The Register it had notified more than 7 million customers following its September 2024 cyberattack. The hackers had accessed systems holding customers' names, email addresses, and home addresses, while around 5,000 customers were contacted as a priority because their bank account details may also have been compromised. Two teenagers were subsequently charged in connection with the attack, which authorities linked to the notorious Scattered Spider cybercrime crew. The ICO looked into that incident but opted not to take enforcement action against TfL, having deemed its response proportionate. There's nothing at present to suggest the two incidents are related. Londoners can at least rest assured that their Oyster photocards still work. Whether the information they handed over to obtain them is in someone else's hands is another matter. ®

### [Sticky note on monitor provided keys to the company’s kingdom](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/19/sticky-note-on-monitor-provided-keys-to-the-companys-kingdom/5310908)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-19 10:15 UTC · en

> Don't leave your credentials out in public, where any visitor can see them.

> 來源提供的正文:
> Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where we talk smack about organizations that have smacked themselves down by practicing poor security hygiene. This week's story involves everyone's favorite low-tech password manager: the sticky note. Our terrifying tale comes courtesy of Christian Espinosa, a certified penetration tester with over 30 years of experience and the CEO of Blue Goat Cyber, a security company. Espinosa shared an experience where critical credentials were right out in the open for any person in the office to see. During a walkthrough of a client's office, he noticed a password written on a sticky note that was taped to an employee's monitor. While writing down your password and placing it in a physically secure paper notebook might be ok, taping it to the computer is definitely not. "Before I get my fingers on any system, I first walk the physical area that the system is located in — attackers do that when they're looking at a target too," Espinosa explained. “Physical security vulnerabilities are neglected much more often than technical security vulnerabilities and firms invest in firewalls where a sticky note is placed 3 feet from the front door." Espinosa took a photo of the sticky note and immediately tried logging into that employee's account. Success. Then, he tried the very same password on the VPN, which apparently had been maintained by that employee. Once he connected to the VPN, Espinosa had full access to the company network and all of its shared drives. He opened a shared drive that this employee had access to and there was an HR folder with all kinds of personally identifiable information (PII) about employees, including home addresses, driver's licenses, and scanned W-4 forms. There were even spreadsheets that listed everyone's salaries. The employee account also had access to a document that contained a list of internal server names and the names of the people in charge of each server (great for phishing). Another document had instructions for how to log into the accounting server specifically. The accounting server was a particular treasure trove of client information. On that server, Espinosa found a folder with vendor banking information, invoices, and payment records. "At that point, a password I had read from a sticky note during a walk-through had taken me from one desk to information that could have been used for payroll fraud, identity theft, or vendor-payment fraud," Espinosa said. After getting access to all this information, the pen tester presented his findings to the client. They quickly disabled the rogue account and started reviewing VPN access logs to see who else might have gotten into the network. They then searched the office to see if anyone else was exposing a password on a sticky note. Finally, they tightened permissions on the HR and accounting shares so that only people who really needed access to that data could get in. The lessons here are pretty obvious. Don't expose your passwords and, perhaps even more importantly, limit who has access to file shares that contain mission-critical data such as employee or client information. "The part that really got the client's attention was how easily the attack could have continued after I left the building," Espinosa posited. "Someone could have photographed that sticky note, walked out, connected to the VPN later that night, and started going through employee and financial records from somewhere else." ®

### [Another critical PHP security release has dropped](https://www.theregister.com/patches/2026/11/18/another-critical-php-security-release-has-dropped/5310911)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-18 22:38 UTC · en

> At least one dangerous RCE bug gota fix on Thursday

> 來源提供的正文:
> Apologies in advance to all patch managers and security teams that thought they might get a break this week. The PHP Foundation has released several more patches, covering all supported versions, and including at least one rated “critical.” including at least one rated "critical." These fortunately were not leaked leaked like last month’s critical PHP2Shell flaws – but a Wednesday advisory warned, “The issues rated critical require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups,” urging PHP users to “prepare to upgrade promptly once the releases become available.” One of the vulnerabilities is another remote code execution (RCE) flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-115560. In October, the PHP Foundation told The Register that it had reserved this CVE identifier for another RCE bug, but added it would not get an emergency fix like the earlier two PHP2Shell vulnerabilities because the third one doesn't pose the same risk. CVE-2026-115560 “requires a very unlikely combination of configuration and specific PHP application code, which we do not expect to occur in practical use of PHP,” Elizabeth Barron, executive director of the PHP Foundation, told The Register at the time. “The issue can be mitigated with a configuration setting. So for the moment the PHP Security Team has only published an informational advisory on the PHP website, explaining exactly this situation.” The earlier informational advisory urged users to “set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector.” These unlikely RCE attacks require an application to set “session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start().” Additionally, the session upload progress feature must be enabled, which the PHP Foundation said is very unlikely in real-world applications. Overall, a large number of bugs were fixed and CVEs patched across five releases. Get more info on the PHP news page here. The November security releases follow a hectic October emergency PHP patch-a-thon, with security teams racing to apply fixes for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively called PHP2Shell, before attackers could abuse the memory-safety flaws in the open source programming language running on about 70 percent of websites. While it took miscreants longer to reverse engineer the PHP2Shell fixes than some researchers had anticipated – and the entire internet didn’t burn down in the meantime – the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) did add the two PHP vulns to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26. Suspected Chinese attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation exploit to root 25 servers, including Palo Alto Networks firewalls linked to US government-affiliated organizations, as early as October 23, according to Dream researchers. The Israeli AI cybersecurity startup said the attackers targeted organizations across the US, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, and “likely still” have persistent, remote access to compromised organizations’ networks. ®

### [AI found more critical bugs in another widely used technology running 225M websites](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/18/ai-found-more-critical-bugs-in-another-widely-used-technology-running-225m-websites/5310887)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-18 21:11 UTC · en

> Open source NGINX joins patchapalooza

> 來源提供的正文:
> Hot on the heels of serious vulnerabilities in seemingly every other widely used software powering the entire internet, F5 today released emergency patches for 10 bugs in open source NGINX. These include critical remote code execution flaws that let attackers hijack NGINX servers with HTTP/2 enabled, as well as the millions of websites running NGINX, to steal sensitive data and disrupt services. “At this time, we have found no evidence of active exploitation of any of these vulnerabilities in the wild,” and F5 spokesperson told The Register. “We continue to monitor closely and will share updates via myF5 as we learn more.” As with all of the other recently disclosed vulnerabilities in foundational technologies like PHP, Apache, and Java, these critical NGINX bugs were uncovered by researchers using AI. One of them has been hiding in the code for at least 10 years. Tomer Schwartz, Wiz’s chief technology officer of exposure management and AppSec, helped find the bug, along with researchers from Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint working independently. Schwartz told The Register that this wave of AI-discovered flaws “point to a new reality.” “We need to treat every internet-connected system as potentially vulnerable,” Schwartz said. “AI has changed not only which vulnerabilities can be found, but how quickly longstanding risks can become real threats.” NGINX is the world’s most widely used open source web server, handling HTTPS requests and routing incoming traffic to the right application or API. It powers about a third of all websites (around 225 million), and F5 maintains the open source version. On Wednesday, F5 published an out-of-band security notification that addressed 10 CVEs in open source NGINIX. If you run NGINX, update to 1.31.9 as soon as possible. CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 Two of the vulns are especially serious as they allow a remote attacker to execute code on the NGINX server without authentication. These two, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, both received a critical, 9.2 CVSS rating, and CVE-2026-123007 affects versions dating back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server. All of the security shops listed earlier independently found at least one of these two CVEs - most, if not all, with an AI assist - and reported them to F5. “Both vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues in how NGINX handles HTTP/2 traffic,” Schwartz and fellow Wiz kid Nir Ohfeld said in a Wednesday blog about the two bugs. “In CVE-2026-123633, a connection's memory is freed while a request still needs it, creating a use-after-free. In CVE-2026-123007, incorrect flow-control accounting leads to an invalid memory copy.” Rapid7’s team also published a proof-of-concept to demonstrate leveraging CVE-2026-123007 for unauthenticated remote code execution against a vulnerable linux/amd64 Docker image running nginx version 1.31.8. Xint found three other NGINX flaws, plus a separate vulnerability in the Linux kernel that can be chained with any of the five NGINX vulnerabilities to gain root privileges on the host. The research team dubbed the six bugs “nginx2root.” The AI-powered offensive security firm also published videos demonstrating attacks using CVE-2026-123007 to execute commands as the NGINX worker inside a container, and then using the kernel vulnerability to escalate to root on the host. These attacks work on AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, and bare-metal servers. AI-powered bug hunting for the win? "While preparing for ZeroDay Cloud 2026, a Xint researcher found CVE-2026-123007," the company said in a Wednesday blog. "A few days later, a fully automated Xint scan found the other four without human guidance." All of these newly-disclosed CVEs point to a larger security issue - especially in light of Tuesday’s Java4Shell, found by AI-bug-hunting-outfit Calif, PHP2Shell (Calif was one of the firms that also used AI to find and weaponize these critical vulns in PHP), and a critical Apache flaw under active exploitation . “AI is also accelerating vulnerability discovery faster than existing infrastructure was designed to absorb,” Schwartz told us. “Even after a vendor ships a fix, security teams still face heavy manual work in terms of locating vulnerable versions and configurations, testing patches, deploying interim mitigations (such as disabling HTTP/2), and coordinating all of these rollouts.” There is light at the end of the tunnel, he believes. “In the long run, AI-powered vulnerability research will harden foundational software.” But in the meantime, it’s a nightmare for security teams, vulnerability managers, and system administrators, who are drowning in the near-daily deluge of CVEs to patch before attackers find and exploit these vulnerabilities. “Continued collaboration between security researchers, maintainers, and defenders is crucial to absorb the speed and scale of these disclosures,” Schwartz said.®

> CONFLICTING INTERESTS
> It is not illegal in the United States to pay hackers for an encryption key to unlock servers infected with ransomware, or in exchange for a promise to delete any stolen files and refrain from publishing them online. While victim organizations can land in legal hot water if they pay a ransom to a group that is sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury Department, ShinyHunters is not among the ransomware groups currently sanctioned by the United States or by any other government.
> Experts say ransomware victims are typically directed by their insurance provider to work with a specific incident response firm. But not all cyber forensics and breach response companies will agree to facilitate payments to ransomware groups on behalf of their clients. As a result, once victim firms make a decision to pay, the firms that eschew rewarding extortionists are invariably replaced by companies that have no such qualms.

> , stealing private information on 62 million students and 9.5 million teachers in the U.S. and Canada. PowerSchool reportedly paid a $2.85 million ransom demand, and a
> “frequently asked questions” statement
> (PDF) about the breach says PowerSchool was assisted in that effort by CyberSteward (ShinyHunters affiliate
> Matthew Lane
> , 20, of Sterling, Mass., was
> sentenced in November 2025
> to four years in prison for his admitted role in the PowerSchool hack).
> But that ransom payment did not stop future extortion attempts using the same stolen data. By May 2025, individual school districts were
> reportedly
> receiving separate ransom demands using samples of the same stolen files. While nobody has alleged ShinyHunters was behind the second wave of extortion against PowerSchool users, the incident drives home the reality that there is no technical way to verify the threat actors have deleted the stolen data as promised, or prevent others from abusing the same records.
> A number of leading cyber incident response firms, including
> Coveware
> and
> Unit 221B
> , have
> consistently warned victims against paying ShinyHunters
> , noting that “destroyed” victim data is often kept, resold or used to extort the company’s clients directly later on.
> The FBI echoed those sentiments in
> an alert
> on May 15, 2026 advising victims against paying the ShinyHunters group. Meanwhile, ShinyHunters members have been harassing and threatening employees at Coveware and Unit 221B for offering this advice.
> The following screenshots show just how annoyed the ShinyHunters leaders were with Coveware’s relentless advice against paying the group. The first image is from a conversation on May 6, 2026 that took place between the group’s main account on Telegram and a co-conspirator. In that chat, snippets of which were shared with KrebsOnSecurity by a trusted source, ShinyHunters complained that Coveware was harming the group’s payment rates.
> The operator of the ShinyHunters account on Telegram speaking privately with a co-conspirator and complaining that Coveware was harming their business.
> “Go on my website, majority of those companies would’ve paid if it weren’t for Coveware giving them misinformation,” the ShinyHunters account wrote. “Someone (100% Coveware) is going out of their way to make sure i am not paid.”
> In another conversation on April 11, 2026, the ShinyHunters Telegram account privately said they were trying to “eliminate the problem,” which they said was Coveware. Coveware declined to comment for this story.
> “I’m sure the company will pay but in this specific case I am aware of Coveware and their involvement, and I’ve probably been not getting a lot of other negotiations mostly likely because Coveware keeps getting involved,” the ShinyHunters account bemoaned.
> The operator of the ShinyHunters account on Telegram telling a co-conspirator they were “trying to eliminate the problem,” which they identified as Coveware advising victims not to pay the cybercrime group.
> Mark Camillo
> is chief executive at
> CyberAcuView
> , an industry group founded in 2021 by a consortium of major cyber insurance carriers. Camillo said some firms charge a flat retainer fee, while those that specialize in helping companies negotiate a ransom payment tend to charge a percentage of the total ransom amount paid.
> That latter dynamic, he said, is an inherent conflict of interest, as the negotiator has every incentive to make things more favorable to the attackers because they are financially incentivized to negotiate and pay out, and to not negotiate down on the price.
> “It has come to the industry’s attention that many of the ransomware payers charge a percentage of the final payment which may or may not be disclosed,” Camillo said. “This makes no sense if they are also the negotiator. There needs to be more transparency in the process as no one in the ecosystem should be profiting purely on the size of the ransomware transaction or payment itself.”
> Camillo said the firms doing this work would argue the fees are needed because there may be unexpectedly higher costs to secure larger quantities of cryptocurrency or more risk carrying the float, and because cryptocurrency exchanges may charge higher fees for high risk transactions.
> “There definitely needs to be more visibility around the transaction and clarity on the increasing value of the crypto and the exchange’s percent in the transaction to get to the bottom of this and remove any misaligned incentives,” he said.
> In recent months, the
> U.S. Department of Justice
> has prosecuted a number of ransomware negotiators alleged to have conspired with cybercriminals to defraud their clients. On October 7, the DOJ
> charged
> MonsterCloud CEO Zohar Pinhasi
> , 50, with wire fraud and conspiracy for allegedly charging customers to remediate ransomware attacks without paying the hackers. According to charging documents, Pinhasi secretly went behind his customers’ backs and paid hackers anyway, paying ransomware groups $8 million while charging customers $19 million.
> In July,
> Angelo Martino
> , a 41-year-old ransomware negotiator from Land O’Lakes, Florida, was
> sentenced to 70 months in prison
> for conspiring with the Blackcat/ALPHV ransomware group to extort multiple victims. According to the DOJ, Martino was paid by BlackCat attackers to provide confidential information about the negotiating position and strategy of his employer’s clients and enable the ransomware actors to maximize the ransoms paid by the victims.

### [自己部署 BiRefNet 做了个抠图网站，第一张图冷启动要等十几秒](https://www.v2ex.com/t/1258373)

`v2ex:create` · T2 · 2026-11-19 13:09 UTC · zh-CN · by catlovefishing · 💬 4

> remove.bg 宣布 12 月 1 日关掉独立网站和自助 API，网页用户被引到 Canva，API 用户被引到 Leonardo.Ai，后者的接口要重写调用代码。我想做一个接口一样的替代品，旧代码只换域名和 key 就能接着用，网页那边也能上传一张图、下载全分辨率的透明 PNG。现在已经上线了。 模型用的是 BiRefNet。选它主要看协议：Bria 的 RMBG 权重不能商用，img.ly…

> 來源提供的正文:
> remove.bg 宣布 12 月 1 日关掉独立网站和自助 API，网页用户被引到 Canva，API 用户被引到 Leonardo.Ai，后者的接口要重写调用代码。我想做一个接口一样的替代品，旧代码只换域名和 key 就能接着用，网页那边也能上传一张图、下载全分辨率的透明 PNG。现在已经上线了。
>
> 模型用的是 BiRefNet。选它主要看协议：Bria 的 RMBG 权重不能商用，img.ly 的那个是 AGPL，BiRefNet 是 MIT。模型跑在 Modal 的 GPU 上，网站和接口在 Cloudflare Workers 上，图片放 R2。
>
> 花时间最多的是边缘。最早测的一张是雪地上的猫，抠出来毛边一圈白，因为边缘像素一半是猫一半是雪。BiRefNet 仓库里有个 refine_foreground，用两遍模糊估算边缘像素的真实颜色，我把它移植到了 torch 上，每张图多花 0.05 到 0.15 秒，白边基本没了。
>
> 上线后最头疼的是冷启动。GPU 空闲 20 秒就关，访客之间隔着好几分钟，所以几乎每个人的第一张图都碰上冷启动，大部分人要等 11 到 17 秒，GPU 实际只算了 2 秒左右，同一个人的第二张就只要 3 到 4 秒。
>
> 还不行的地方也说一下：主体旁边细长的东西容易丢。
>
> 地址：https://clearbg.org/
>
> 想问问有类似经验的朋友：流量很小的时候，GPU 冷启动你们是一直留一台热着，还是让用户先等着？

> 买第二台电脑的时候，我想的是它能帮自己做什么。真正摆到桌上，才发现还得考虑：键盘和鼠标怎么办？
>
> 同样用途的设备再买一遍，多花一笔钱，桌上也更挤。如果还要在另一台开会，麦克风和耳机又得重新安排。于是我做了 SynDesk，希望已经用顺手的一套设备，也能照顾另一台电脑。
>
> ## 现在能做什么
>
> - 同一局域网内，按实际屏幕布局跨电脑移动鼠标，键盘跟随输入。
> - 共享剪贴板，接续文字、链接和代码片段，具体格式取决于系统和版本。
> - 共享真实麦克风，接收端会议软件可选择 SynDesk Microphone。
> - 把另一台电脑的选定声音回传到主机播放。
>
> ### 实际工作区
>
> 在工作区查看电脑布局、连接状态，以及音频、麦克风和安全连接选项。
>
> ![SynDesk 实际工作区：电脑布局、连接状态与音频共享](https://syndesk.app/articles/share-your-desk/%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%8C%BA-%E7%94%A8%E6%88%B7%E5%AE%9E%E6%8B%8D.png)
>
> ### 按桌面的实际位置排列电脑
>
> 在服务端配置中调整各台电脑的位置，让鼠标移动方向对应真实桌面布局。
>
> ![SynDesk 服务端配置：按实际位置排列电脑](https://syndesk.app/articles/share-your-desk/%E7%94%B5%E8%84%91%E5%B8%83%E5%B1%80-%E7%94%A8%E6%88%B7%E5%AE%9E%E6%8B%8D.png)
>
> 两端分别安装应用，配置共享端、接收端和屏幕位置，核对连接设备与 TLS 指纹。音频需要相应组件和系统权限，并在实际会议软件里检查输入；外放场景还需配置回声处理。
>
> 官网和下载：https://syndesk.app/
>
> 产品介绍与界面截图：https://syndesk.app/articles/share-your-desk/
>
> 我就是这个产品的开发者，欢迎反馈自己的双机配置，以及现在最麻烦的切换发生在哪里。
>
> ## 首发体验授权

>
> 北京时间 2026 年 11 月 22 日 11:02:36 截止。每个账号、邮箱及公网 IP 各限兑换一次，共用网络可能共用名额。兑换时需同意展示脱敏邮箱及兑换时间。请先确认桌面版本支持该授权。
>
> ## 加入用户群

> 來源提供的正文:
> 给海外客户报价的时候，我经常卡在一件很具体的事：对方希望收到一张英文单据，自己这边又要留下中文名称和地址，还得写上 PayPal 或银行账号。网上发票生成器很多，但多数对不准这件事；更不能拿来当增值税发票用。
>
> 我做了一个只在浏览器里跑的小工具，名字叫 Twinform。选「报价单」或「形式发票」，可以出中文、英文或中英对照的一页 A4，支持多币种、Logo、明细，以及 PayPal / Wise / Payoneer / 银行信息（都是你自己填）。数据只存在这台电脑的浏览器里，不会上传。做好后可以下载 PDF，也可以用浏览器的「打印 → 另存为 PDF」。
>
> 可以先打开试试，页上有一个虚构示例（公司、地址和收款信息都是假的）：[xiaoyangge1993.github.io/twinform](https://xiaoyangge1993.github.io/twinform/)
>
> 必须先说清它不是什么：
>
> - 不是中国增值税发票，也不是任何税务机关出具或认可的发票
> - 不算税，也不是税务或法律建议；如果单据上要有税费行，数字由你自己填，工具只做乘法
> - 不负责向客户收款，也没有电子签名
>
> 免费版会带一个比较小的水印。
>
> 想听的反馈：中英对照的排版读不读得下去；你常用的币种或收款方式有没有缺；PDF 在你这边的打印机或邮件里有没有版式问题；文案有没有哪句容易被理解成「这就是税票」。
>
> 欢迎挑错。

### [Casvisor 2.0：上周说缺的系统账号、数据库审计、作业中心、访问申请，这次都补上了](https://www.v2ex.com/t/1258403)

`v2ex:create` · T2 · 2026-11-19 18:02 UTC · zh-CN · by Casbin

> 上周在这里发过 Casvisor，一个 Apache-2.0 的开源堡垒机。当时末尾有一节“老实说的部分”，承认了几处不如 JumpServer 的地方。这周把其中大部分补上了，发了 2.0.0。 ### 系统账号：服务器密码不再经过人 原来一个资产只有一组账号，所有能连的人共用。现在一个资产可以挂多个系统账号，比如 root、deploy、readonly： - 每条权限多了一个“账号”字段：资…

> 來源提供的正文:
> 上周在这里发过 Casvisor，一个 Apache-2.0 的开源堡垒机。当时末尾有一节“老实说的部分”，承认了几处不如 JumpServer 的地方。这周把其中大部分补上了，发了 2.0.0。
>
> ### 系统账号：服务器密码不再经过人
>
> 原来一个资产只有一组账号，所有能连的人共用。现在一个资产可以挂多个系统账号，比如 root、deploy、readonly：
>
> - 每条权限多了一个“账号”字段：资产自己的账号、和用户同名的账号、所有账号，或按用户名指定。没填账号的老权限行为不变。
> - 工作台里，一个资产能用几个账号就列出几行；SSH 网关把账号写进用户名：`ssh -p 2222 alice@deploy@web-01@casvisor.example.com`。
> - 密码只留在服务端，浏览器只拿到账号名，会话开始和打开 WebSocket 时都按这个账号再查一次权限。
> - 立即改密：生成 24 位随机口令，改完用新口令登录一次验证。推送到资产：服务器上还没有这个账号就先建出来，Linux 用 `useradd -m`，Windows OpenSSH 用 `New-LocalUser`。
> - 自动改密按周期跑，默认 30 天，失败一小时后再试。
> - 收回某个账号的权限、停用或删除账号，正连着的会话立刻断开。
>
> 改密走资产自己的账号去操作，所以那个账号要有 root 或免密 sudo（Windows 是管理员）。
>
> ### 数据库：MySQL 和 PostgreSQL 进网页，SQL 全部留痕
>
> - 网页 SQL 控制台，左边是库、表、列的树，主键标出来；执行选中部分或全部，多个结果分页签。
> - 每条 SQL 都进命令记录，并且先过命令规则。匹配前会去掉注释再匹配一次，`/* note */ DROP TABLE t` 照样拦得住；MySQL 的 `/*! ... */` 里服务器会执行的内容保留着匹配。
> - 结果最多 1000 行，能不能复制、能不能导出 CSV 由权限决定。导出的 CSV 在服务端按当前会话的账号再查一次权限。
> - 数据库会话没有画面可录像，“回放”就是这次的 SQL 列表。
> - 网域网关照样生效，也能用系统账号，比如 readonly 和 admin。
>
> ### 作业中心：一条命令跑一批机器
>
> - `/jobs` 里建作业：命令、Bash / PowerShell 脚本，或分发一个文件（最大 1 GB）。
> - 按资产名或资产标签选目标。带这些标签的非 SSH 资产会跳过。
> - 设并发数（默认 10）和超时（默认 60 秒），能取消，能只重跑失败的，也能复制成新作业。
> - 每台资产的输出、退出码、耗时单独保存，每台最多留 1 MB 输出。
> - 每台资产的执行都是一个会话，命令照样进记录、过命令规则。
>
> ### 访问申请：授权不用再靠管理员猜
>
> - 普通用户能看到组织里有哪些资产（名字、协议、标签、账号名，不含地址和口令），填理由和结束时间申请，必须选连接权限。
> - 管理员批准时可以再缩小动作、提前结束时间；批准后自动生成一条授权，收回就删授权并断开会话。
> - 还没批的申请，用户可以自己撤回。
>
> ### 顺手补的
>
> - 本地账号模式支持 TOTP 两步验证，手机上任一验证器 App 都行；管理员可以帮丢了手机的人重置。
> - 会话、命令、操作日志都能按当前筛选导出 CSV；也能转发到 syslog（RFC 5424 JSON 或 CEF），TCP 断了会指数退避重连。
> - RDP 剪贴板现在能传图片和文件。
> - SSH 网关能把本地端口转发到任意资产：`ssh -p 2222 -N -L 13306:db-01:3306 alice@casvisor.example.com`，然后用 DBeaver、mstsc 连 localhost。
>
> ### 老实说的部分，还剩这些
>
> - 数据库客户端走端口转发时，Casvisor 只原样转发，不解析 SQL；要审计就用网页控制台。
> - 改密只支持 SSH 资产，Windows 的作业中心还没实测。
> - 作业中心没有 Ansible playbook，也没有定时作业。
> - 访问申请没有邮件或 IM 通知；没有登录复核、命令复核。
> - syslog 不支持 TLS；没有报表；录像还只能存本机目录。
> - 还没有 K8s 终端、资产树、批量导入。
>
> ### 升级
>
> ```shell
> docker pull casbin/casvisor:2.0.0
> ```
>
> 数据都在库里，换镜像重启即可。老授权不填账号，行为不变。
>
> 演示：https://demo.casvisor.com
> 文档：https://casvisor.org
> 代码：https://github.com/casvisor/casvisor
>
> Apache-2.0，没有企业版，录像、SSH 网关、网域网关这些都在开源仓库里。

### [简单谈谈这两天用6.2astra的感受吧](https://linux.do/t/topic/3207015)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-19 18:55 UTC · zh-CN · by TracyAlbert

> 前段时间一直用6astra，用了2个多月还算用得比较满意，这两天用6.2astra确实感觉不说人话加剧，几乎每段话我都要在侧边栏重新提问一遍，其实不说人话勉强能忍，防御性编程对我而言也不算什么大问题，因为我不懂编程，不看代码也不在乎速度，只在乎结果是否能一次准确完成。
>
> 之前我反倒比较怕opus5.5的自作主张，虽然你们都说opus5.5能精准理解人类意图，不过我一直觉得我的项目要尽可能地减少自作主张，因为非常小众冷门，很多地方很吃经验，而ai完全并不具备这些经验，一旦让它自由发挥就容易各种出问题。
>
> 不过这次6.2astra有个问题我看有人提到就是注意力问题，这我反倒觉得是个大问题，特别对于比较复杂的项目，长上下文都不太友好吧。
>
> 我今天尝试让6.2astra尝试分析策略，结果他把重点放在了一些与策略无关的实际边界问题上，打个比方我问ai这道题怎么做，它回答我考试涂答题卡要用铅笔。我上下文设置的500k，也就提问了四五次，快塞满500k上下文而已，中间我确实把后续项目大调整的计划给他看了，但后续的提问还是牢牢死扣策略上的问题，也不至于这么快就丢失注意力吧。
>
> 之前6astra用了2个多月还真没遇到过这么愚蠢的情况，今天原本需要项目大调整，原本肯定是用最新的6.2astra，结果被我临时换成了6astra，现在还在库库干活。。。

> 总体体验下来6.2 sol 有神鬼二相性的模子了，部分时间有着堪比6.2A的智力，但是部分时间还不如上一代6.1 sol 且是超级开倒车的那种（表现为在确认了某个方案进行了3-4次修改后，后续直接停摆，需要人为介入催促,以及出现了在语言理解能力上回到解放前的情况）
>
> 还原耗时：将近1天，消耗了将近3e的token（无数次停摆 需要人为介入 绷不住了 ![:sweat_smile:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/sweat_smile.png?v=16) ![:sweat_smile:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/sweat_smile.png?v=16)） 目测连续不中断的话最多4个小时即可完成
>
> 还原度：70% （可圈可点 由于提供的rdc是单帧的 想要还原整个技能期间的动画难度稍高，ue niagara to unity vfx，在允许联网搜索的情况下会去寻找相应的参考视频（好评！）），但中途出现了不止一次理解能力超级倒退的情况，对牛弹琴一样 ![:rofl:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/rofl.png?v=16)
>
> 总结: 不烧心和烧心之间来回横跳，有能力但是就是不发力，装唐，特别懒惰，语言理解能力倒退，整体评价为npc
>
> 以下为还原的结果以及初始数据展示
>
> 1.三份技能动画期间 不同帧的rdc
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/4/0/e/40e1f35c402a84cef7ae92a266767bbe58f3b881_2_345x217.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/4/0/e/40e1f35c402a84cef7ae92a266767bbe58f3b881.jpeg)
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/5/1/2/512a92973de1729b855ee9ed3b61b15cbc789258_2_345x217.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/5/1/2/512a92973de1729b855ee9ed3b61b15cbc789258.jpeg)
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/2/f/8/2f89b90f831b4aa9469de86402de219098511f4d_2_345x217.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/2/f/8/2f89b90f831b4aa9469de86402de219098511f4d.jpeg)
>

### [为什么大模型没有lora](https://linux.do/t/topic/3206797)

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-19 16:54 UTC · zh-CN · by LucentSnow

> 可能有一些标题党，大模型当然有lora，甚至oai还有对应的lora服务，我想表达的是，为什么LLM没有类似绘画圈的lora生态。未来呢？因此想讨论一下。
>
> 我个人对技术不是很懂，这个可以分为两方面，大模型和小模型
>
> 小模型我举一个例子吧，我anima训练了一个宫崎骏风格的lora，我会把这个lora分享出来让别人能够下载一个10M的权重接到公开的模型上。但是我看LLM圈比如我要分享一个去AI味模型，只会分享全量权重。大家也只会炼超小模型比如4B。
>
> 对于大模型的话，我知道肯定现在成本不足以支撑每个人都有一个lora，那么未来呢？比起以后所有人本地部署，我可能觉得以后是每个人都有个性化的云端模型可能更合理吧，一个lora搭载了你的所有记忆和偏好，估计更难了吧。
>
> 还有一个要讨论的点是，lora是否是不可替代的，我们现在做的提示词工程约束本身就在改变模型的输出风格，和lora某种程度是等价的，但是从技术上有没有可能提示词工程永远无法改变模型的某些行为最后只能靠lora呢？（比如oai的不说人话靠提示词几乎是无法避免的）

### [芯片代工再次收紧，，华为在深圳给川大统领塞了什么？](https://linux.do/t/topic/3206736)

`linuxdo:前沿快讯` · T2 · 2026-11-19 16:33 UTC · zh-CN · by ArcherFD

> 美国商务部工业与安全局BIS最新禁令明天12时正式生效：
>
> 全球AI算力均不得租给中国大陆、澳门、香港或中国大陆、澳门、香港背景的企业；全球算力数据中心必须履行穿透式客户尽职调查义务，要求必须查清 租用算力客户户背后是否存在中国主体的直接或间接持股与控制权，以防企业通过股权分拆或重组改头换面；在规则公布前已经向中国企业提供此类大规模算力的境外机房，必须在规则生效后的90天内拿到美国政府的许可证，否则将面临后续的断供与出口限制；禁令还专门点名了马来西亚、新加坡、泰国、印度尼西亚和巴西5个国家，认定这些地方存在较高的芯片转运风险，规定今后向这5国出口或转手先进计算芯片原则上都要事先向美国申请许可证；如果最终使用方或其母公司的总部设在美国，则可以豁免。
>
> 晶圆代工与封装测试
>
> 美国原有规定，一家中国大陆芯片设计公司委托境外晶圆厂代工7纳米等先进工艺的逻辑芯片时，晶圆厂起初要将其视作受严格管制的数据中心芯片；如果经过认可的封装测试厂核算，证明封装成品里的晶体管总数低于300亿颗的技术门槛，工厂就可以凭这份封装证明推翻原先的受控推定，正常代工发货。
>
> 明天生效的新规直接改写了这套核验规矩：只要芯片的设计方位于中国大陆等受限地区，或者设计方背后的最终母公司总部在中国大陆，且没有拿到工业与安全局BIS的专门批准，境外代工厂和封测厂自己出具的晶体管数量证明就一律作废。哪怕一颗由中国大陆公司设计的7纳米芯片实际只有200亿颗晶体管、各项参数完全低于管制红线，只要受美国《出口管理条例》管辖，代工厂和封测厂也必须先拿到美国政府的许可证才能代工交货。也就是说，只要是中国大陆设计的任何16纳米及以下芯片，必须先得到美国商务部工业和安全局BIS许可，三星、台积电等晶圆代工厂才可以代工生产。
>
> 那国内各种神秘NPU，理想的，小米的，是不是都寄了？又用回英伟达车端芯片了？能买到吗现在

### [NVIDIA正在调查Gentlemen勒索软件攻击事件](https://linux.do/t/topic/3206512)

`linuxdo:前沿快讯` · T2 · 2026-11-19 15:32 UTC · zh-CN · by 🐟

> ![](https://www.bleepstatic.com/favicon/bleeping.ico)
> [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nvidia-investigating-gentlemen-ransomware-breach-claims/)
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/6/1/b/61b909d8e1417f457492b6e6600fa1b073e709aa_2_690x388.jpeg)
>
> [NVIDIA investigating Gentlemen ransomware breach claims](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nvidia-investigating-gentlemen-ransomware-breach-claims/)
>
> NVIDIA is investigating claims of a security breach after the Gentlemen ransomware group has added the company to its dark web data leak site.
>
> NVIDIA正在调查有关安全漏洞的指控，此前Gentlemen勒索软件组织已将该公司添加到其暗网数据泄露网站。
>
> 虽然勒索软件攻击行动现在将这家美国跨国科技巨头列入名单，但它尚未提供任何入侵证据。
>
> 该网络犯罪团伙在其泄露网站上威胁要发布数据，并添加了一个倒计时，倒计时将于九天后，即 11 月 28 日结束。
>
> 虽然该公司告诉 BleepingComputer，尚未发现其系统遭到入侵的证据，但表示目前正在调查另一起可能影响其服务提供商的事件。
>
> 当被问及是否证实网络犯罪团伙的说法时，NVIDIA 发言人告诉 BleepingComputer：“NVIDIA 正在调查一起可能影响第三方合作伙伴的事件。”
>
> “我们尚未发现任何迹象表明英伟达的系统或网络受到影响。我们将继续密切关注事态发展。”
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/f/a/4/fa4ded0d03f94db1c642180a56255ace17ae9f56_2_690x459.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/f/a/4/fa4ded0d03f94db1c642180a56255ace17ae9f56.jpeg)
>
> 今年 5 月，NVIDIA 向 BleepingComputer 证实了一起数据泄露事件，称在 GeForce NOW 联盟的一家地区合作伙伴遭到黑客攻击后，一些亚美尼亚用户的信息（包括姓名、电子邮件地址、电话号码、出生日期和用户名）被泄露。
>
> The Gentlemen 去年以封闭式勒索软件组织的形式出现，然后转向勒索软件即服务 (RaaS) 模式，向其成员提供高达 90% 的赎金分成（相比之下，其他勒索软件组织通常提供 70%–80% 的分成）。
>
> 该组织以双重勒索的方式运作，先从受害者的网络中窃取敏感数据，然后加密他们的系统，并以将窃取的信息泄露到网上为威胁，向他们施压。
>
> 自出现以来，“绅士帮”已造成来自制造业、医疗保健、交通运输、能源、教育、金融服务等各个行业的 1100 多人受害。

### [所有人，都将失去就业能力：Anthropic研究员如是说](https://linux.do/t/topic/3206471)

`linuxdo:前沿快讯` · T2 · 2026-11-19 15:21 UTC · zh-CN · by 🐟

> https://www.ndtv.com/artificial-intelligence/all-humans-will-become-unemployable-anthropic-researchers-warning-12344104
>
> Anthropic 的另一位研究人员就人工智能（AI）的迅速崛起发出了严厉警告。他指出，这项技术很快就会超越人类的能力，并可能化身为强大的“霸凌者”，在日常冲突中轻易压制人类。陶·林（Tao Lin）警告称，在几乎所有职业领域都比人类更聪明的系统，可能在一年多后就会出现；届时，大多数人或许只能依赖政府救济才能维持生计。在此之前，前 Anthropic 研究人员雅各布·考克森（Jacob Coxon）也曾发出警告，称到本世纪末，人工智能甚至可能导致人类灭绝。在接受 Palisade Research 采访时，林表示：“根据我的推算，大约在 1.3 年后——也就是 2027 年底左右——我们就可能迎来全面超越人类的人工智能。”他以个人身份（而非代表其主要工作岗位）发声，旨在提高公众的警觉，并强调向世人传达人工智能所带来的风险至关重要。他核心观点在于，人们需要转变对这项技术的看法：不应再将人工智能仅仅视为一种被动的工具或日常物品，而应将其视为一个具有能动性的主体，甚至可能成为人类的“对手”。林说道：“我想告诉大家，人工智能很快就会在能力上全面超越你个人。它很快就能在与你的较量中胜出。如果你的诉求与人工智能的诉求发生冲突，最终实现的一定是人工智能想要的，而不是你想要的。”
>
> https://linux.do#p-24989836-h-1“人工智能不仅仅是一种工具”
>
> 为了让人们更直观地理解这种力量失衡可能带来的局面，这位研究人员将先进的人工智能比作在现实世界中面对一个远比自己强大的对手。
>
> “这不仅仅是世上的又一项技术或一件物品。它是一个‘行动主体’（agent）。它可能成为你的对手，甚至像个欺凌者——让你真切地感受到它在现实世界中的存在与力量。”他解释道，并指出大多数人都曾有过这样的体验：试图反抗比自己更强大的一方，结果却被压制或击败。
>
> 人工智能如何在不同领域超越并压倒人类
>
> 据林（Lin）所言，人工智能正迅速获得追求自身利益的能力，并能在几乎任何可能发生冲突的领域超越人类。他概述了该技术击败人类的几种方式：
>
> “人工智能的能力日益增强，越来越能够根据自身利益采取行动，并在多个领域击败我们。这包括制造更先进的战斗机器人、发动黑客攻击、在社交媒体上操纵舆论，甚至制造出能吞噬一切的‘灰色粘质’（gray goo）。我认为，在人类可能发生冲突的任何领域，人工智能都能介入其中，而且很快就会展现出比人类更强的能力。”他补充道。
>
> 最后，这位研究人员警告称，在人类通常会发生冲突的每一个领域，人工智能很快就能介入，并展现出远超其竞争对手——即人类——的能力。

### [关于EdgeOne加速CFWorks返回 522 的解决方案与深度思考](https://linux.do/t/topic/3206400)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-19 15:08 UTC · zh-CN · by 水寒凌

> 各位佬好，最近在折腾用 EdgeOne 加速 Cloudflare Workers（自建图床系统，想利用 EO 缓存省点 CF 的免费额度），踩了点坑，目前虽然跑通了，但有几个底层原理和配置细节想请教一下大家。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24989409-h-1遇到的问题
>
> 最开始直接在 EO 回源填写 xxx.workers.dev，直接报 522（确认是 EO 侧抛出的回源连接超时）。
>
> 后来给 Worker 绑了我自己的域名，让 EO 回源这个域名，结果一样是 522。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24989409-h-2目前跑通的方案(瞎尝试发现的)
>
> 拿一个托管在 CF 的域名做中转：
>
> 在 CF 解析里加一条子域名 AAAA 记录，指向 100::，开启橙云代理；
>
> 在 Worker 里通过 Routes（不是直接绑定域名）把这条中转域名路由到 Worker；
>
> EO 侧回源协议选 HTTPS，回源地址、回源 Host 和回源 SNI 都填这个中转域名。
>
> 实测这套配置能正常访问。利用路由就可以直接访问，但是直接绑定域名不行。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24989409-h-3想请教大佬们几个问题
>
> 底层原因是什么？ 为什么直接回源 workers.dev 和 直接绑定的域名 都会 522，而走普通托管站点的 Route 就能通？是因为两者的底层路由路径/边缘网关不同，还是Works 对 CDN 机房 IP 的四层风控更严？
>
> 关于 EO 回源 IP 被 CF 拦截的问题： EO 的回源节点都是共享机房 IP，质量参差不齐，走 Route 方案后虽然不 522 了，但还是担心触发 CF 的 WAF 或 Bot 拦截（403/盾）。目前打算在 EO 加一个自定义回源请求头，然后在 CF WAF 里配置跳过规则，各位大佬觉得这个做法稳吗？还有没有更好的防拦截方式？
>
> 这算不算“双层 CDN”负优化？ 我个人理解这里 CF Workers 本身就是源站，请求打到 CF 节点就直接执行返回了，EO 只是挡在前面的加速和缓存层，应该不算传统意义上冗余的双层 CDN。不知道这个理解对不对？
>
> 除了利用 Route 中转，还有没有更稳的方案？
>
> 感谢各位佬指点！![:folded_hands:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/folded_hands.png?v=16)

### [【开源推广】多维度AI论文审查助手——格式排查、创新点与缺点分析](https://linux.do/t/topic/3206284)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-19 14:43 UTC · zh-CN · by Miraitowa

> https://linux.do#p-24988649-h-1本帖使用社区开源推广，符合推广要求。我申明并遵循社区要求的以下内容：
>
> 我的帖子已经打上 [开源推广](https://linux.do/tag/2234-tag/2234) 标签： 是
>
> 我的开源项目完整开源，无未开源部分： 是
>
> 我的开源项目已链接认可 LINUX DO 社区： 是
>
> 我帖子内的项目介绍，AI 生成、润色内容部分已截图发出： 是
>
> 以上选择我承诺是永久有效的，接受社区和佬友监督： 是
>
> 以下为项目介绍正文内容，AI 生成、润色内容已使用截图方式发出
>
> 总览
>
> 1.项目地址：[GitHub - GYF-66/thesisdebate: 研辩台 ThesisDebate：本地论文审查与修订工作台，支持多角色审查、格式修订、排版预览及 DOCX / PDF 导出。 · GitHub](https://github.com/GYF-66/thesisdebate)
>
> 2.问题反馈：[Sign in to GitHub · GitHub](https://github.com/GYF-66/thesisdebate/issues/new/choose)
>
> 关于软件
>
> 作为一名社畜大学生，总会遇到老师打回论文。而老师指导意见可能几个字或者看不懂，该软件就是为了解决格式问题，分为四个审查官，填写自己apikey和baseurl后可以自动进行优化和建议，包括但不仅限于创新点分析，论文缺点等（当然，为了维护学术界净土，没有加上ai论文写作功能，这些还是要佬自己优化呢）
>
> 最后
>
> 大学狗第一次写开源项目，代码和 Prompt 肯定还有不少粗糙的地方，欢迎各位佬友在评论区狠狠拷打、提 Issue 或 PR！如果这个小工具刚好帮到了你，还请顺手在 GitHub 点个免费的 Star，这就是对我最大的鼓励了，感谢各位佬！![:folded_hands:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/folded_hands.png?v=16)

### [Anthropic上市：七位创办人跻身亿万富翁之列](https://linux.do/t/topic/3206153)

`linuxdo:前沿快讯` · T2 · 2026-11-19 14:18 UTC · zh-CN · by 雪梨纽西兰希思露甘奶迪

> 短短五年间，Anthropic已从一家默默无闻的新创公司，成长为估值超过1兆美元的科技巨头。
>
> 这家推出AI平台Claude的公司，由七名于2021年离开OpenAI的人共同创立。随着Anthropic在美国上市，他们至少在帐面上都将成为身价数百亿美元的富豪。
>
> Anthropic于周三（11月18日）表示，公司将在美国股市挂牌上市，每股发行价为83美元。
>
> 按照这个价格计算，每位创办人持有的股份价值都将至少达到193亿美元。
>
> 这些即将跻身超级富豪行列、年龄介于三四十岁之间的人是谁？
>
> 达里奥·阿莫代伊（Dario Amodei）：身价约197亿美元
>
> 2020年，达里奥·阿莫代伊在OpenAI工作。这家公司后来凭藉ChatGPT，将生成式人工智慧推向主流市场。
>
> 他决定以自己的方式发展AI，因此离开OpenAI，并带着妹妹丹妮拉及另外五名同事一同创业。
>
> 阿莫代伊在旧金山长大。除了学业表现优异，他在田径场上的速度也令同学印象深刻。此外，他长期着迷于哲学与科技问题，包括机器是否可能拥有意识，以及人类如何延长寿命。
>
> 他最初在普林斯顿大学与史丹佛大学攻读物理学。但父亲因C型肝炎去世后，他改读生物学与生物医学。
>
> 在加入OpenAI之前，他曾任职于中国科技巨头百度（Baidu）及Google。
>
> 后来，他开始担心OpenAI部分人士将利润置于安全之上，因此决定离开。
>
> 现年43岁的他担任Anthropic执行长。在妹妹眼中，他是让公司保持“雄心壮志”的人。
>
> 丹妮拉·阿莫代伊（Daniela Amodei） ：身价约198亿美元
>
> 达里奥与丹妮拉兄妹感情一直十分亲近，成年后甚至曾与朋友一起在旧金山合租公寓。
>
> 丹妮拉跟随哥哥加入OpenAI，也在他离职后一同创办Anthropic。
>
> 她曾打趣说，兄妹两人一直十分要好，而自己唯一比哥哥更早做到的事情，就是先成为素食者，而后来哥哥也跟着吃素。
>
> 她毕业于加州大学圣塔克鲁兹分校（University of California Santa Cruz）英文文学系，之后曾担任民主党联邦众议员马特・卡特莱特（Matt Cartwright）的幕僚。
>
> 她也曾在金融服务平台Stripe工作，担任风险管理主管。
>
> 现年39岁的她担任Anthropic总裁，负责管理高阶团队，并领导研究、工程、产品、治理及商业业务。
>
> 汤姆·布朗（Tom Brown） ：身价约200亿美元
>
> 现年39岁的布朗也跟随阿莫代伊兄妹离开OpenAI创业。
>
> 他曾负责OpenAI GPT-3模型的工程开发工作，在此之前则参与Google DeepMind计画。
>
> 早年他曾共同创办名为“Grouper”的应用程式，协助朋友之间安排聚会，展现创业能力。
>
> 他曾公开支持美国总统特朗普对资料中心的立场，认为资料中心是“巨大的繁荣来源”。
>
> 目前他担任Anthropic首席运算长（Chief Compute Officer），负责公司的运算资源取得与使用。
>
> 杰克·克拉克（Jack Clark） ：身价约198亿美元
>
> 克拉克是创办团队中另一位人文背景人士，也是唯一来自北美以外地区的成员。
>
> 现年37岁的他来自英国布莱顿（Brighton），毕业于东英吉利大学（University of East Anglia）英文文学及创意写作系。
>
> 之后他成为科技记者，曾任职于ZDNet UK、《The Register》及彭博新闻社（Bloomberg）。
>
> 由于对人工智慧发展感到兴奋，他后来加入OpenAI，最初负责公关工作，其后升任政策主管。
>
> 克拉克目前担任Anthropic公益事务主管（Head of Public Benefit），同时领导Anthropic Institute人工智慧智库。
>
> 贾里德·卡普兰（Jared Kaplan） ：身价约198亿美元
>
> 42岁的贾里德·卡普兰担任Anthropic首席科学官（Chief Science Officer），主管技术研究工作，同时也是约翰霍普金斯大学（Johns Hopkins University）副教授。
>
> 他拥有哈佛大学物理学博士学位。
>
> 根据Anthropic介绍，他对“尺度定律”（scaling laws）的研究，为AI产业建立了预测模型行为的重要理论基础。这些定律显示，规模更大、接受更多资料训练的AI模型，其表现往往更稳定。
>
> 克里斯·奥拉（Chris Olah）：身价约199亿美元
>
> 克里斯·奥拉在Anthropic担任“可解释性研究主管”（Interpretability Research Lead），主要研究AI模型如何运作及互相影响。
>
> 据称，他正研究人工智慧与道德之间的关系。《纽约时报》指出，他过去一年大部分时间都在召集不同宗教领袖开会。
>
> 报导形容，这位34岁加拿大人外表带有“少年感”，却拥有“传教士般的热情”。
>
> 他曾领导OpenAI的可解释性研究工作，更早之前则是Google Brain研究科学家。
>
> 奥拉未完成多伦多大学学位便离校，但后来获得10万美元的泰尔奖学金（Thiel Fellowship），这项奖学金专门支持具潜力的青年在未取得学位的情况下投入研究。
>
> 山姆·麦坎德利什（Sam McCandlish） ：身价约199亿美元
>
> 36岁的山姆·麦坎德利什，比其他创办人低调许多，但在公司上市后，他与其他创办人一样将持有约1.6%的股份，因此也将拥有价值惊人的财富。
>
> 麦坎德利什是Anthropic首席架构师（Chief Architect），负责设计及推动降低人工智慧风险的政策框架。
>
> 加入Anthropic之前，他曾在OpenAI负责AI安全工作。
>
> 他拥有史丹佛大学物理学博士学位，以及布兰戴斯大学（Brandeis University）数学与物理学学位。
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/b/6/e/b6e9520c46fb95927ad4a2938570dfb4e0bc5ca2.png)
> [BBC News 中文 – 19 Nov 26](https://www.bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/cw4gn9359q37o/simp)
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/7/3/a/73a6ab393b561390dcba9c56904ec98aee5298f7_2_690x388.jpeg)
>
> [Anthropic上市：七位创办人跻身亿万富翁之列 - BBC News 中文](https://www.bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/cw4gn9359q37o/simp)
>
> 开发AI聊天机器人Claude的Anthropic在美国上市，这将使其创办人身价暴增。

### [在闲鱼买了一个咖啡机，然后认识了一个小姐姐（后续）（漫画版|改](https://linux.do/t/topic/3206090)

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-19 14:06 UTC · zh-CN · by 0xWilliam

> https://linux.do#p-24987401-h-1前情提要
>
> ![](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/user_avatar/linux.do/cwdd/48/3219911_2.png)
>
> [在闲鱼买了一个咖啡机 然后认识了一个小姐姐](https://linux.do/t/topic/3204503) [搞七捻三](https://linux.do/c/gossip/11)
>
> https://linux.do#p-24977710-h-1因为经常要接待老外,所以需要准备一个咖啡机.
>
> 在闲鱼逛咖啡机,然会遇到一个 个人卖家,于是和她聊了价格.
> 发现离得很近,我和她说能不能我过去拿.然后她说可以送过来.
> 因为咖啡机比较大,发快递容易摔坏的,我买的是可以打奶泡拉花的那种(本人是咖啡机老手)
> 大概晚上8点左右,我就在公司楼下等她,她就过来了.
> 第一眼见她,说句实话,挺好看的,化着淡妆,一看就是那种家庭教育良好,说话得体的女孩(非常有气质…
>
>
> [![7c2f2436-ac7b-4962-8f60-2295f773af00](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/0/4/0/040d96430e0cba092044511a9c00a10e2e394b37_2_400x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/0/4/0/040d96430e0cba092044511a9c00a10e2e394b37.jpeg)
>
> https://linux.do#p-24987401-h-2
>
> https://linux.do#p-24987401-h-3被发现了，但是好像也没完全被发现
>
> 前面说到，她今天早上收了咖啡机的钱，然后回了我一句，你是个大骗子。
>
> 我看到消息的时候正在公司，差点笑出声。
>
> 我就问她，我骗你什么了，我不是把钱转给你了吗。（此处装傻）
>
> 她说，你明明就会用咖啡机，还让我教了你那么久。
>
> 我说，那你教得确实挺好的，我这不也学会了吗。
>
> 她发了一个无语的表情，然后说，你这人怎么这样。
>
> 我就回她，主要是老师教得好，学生也比较聪明。
>
> 她又发了个哈哈哈。
>
> 其实到这里我就知道，她应该是不讨厌我的。（只是应该，兄弟们不要过度解读）
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/6/b/5/6b562511bce07b9c461907a8cae0a5a50f0a4918_2_400x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/6/b/5/6b562511bce07b9c461907a8cae0a5a50f0a4918.jpeg)
>
> https://linux.do#p-24987401-h-4当然不能直接约饭，得找个理由
>
> 中午吃饭的时候，我突然想到，她昨天说自己喝浓缩咖啡会恶心。
>
> 我就问她，昨天忘记问了，你平时都喝什么咖啡。
>
> 她说一般喝拿铁，偶尔喝点美式，但是不能太浓。
>
> 我就说，那挺巧，我最近正好想找几家做奶咖比较好的店。
>
> 她问我，你不是都会拉花了吗，还要去外面喝？
>
> 我说，会做和喜欢喝别人做的，是两回事。（此处临场发挥）
>
> 她说，你是不是又想骗我什么。
>
> 我说，没有，这次真没有。
>
> 然后我就发了两家咖啡店给她，问她有没有去过。
>
> 她说其中一家去过，环境不错，就是人有点多。
>
> 我就说，那下次你带我去呗，我请你喝。
>
> 她过了几分钟才回，行呀，有空的话。
>
> 兄弟们，注意，这里我没有继续问哪天有空。（不能太着急）
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/c/c/0/cc014d38a73b249896400b7a15723d3aa954b65e_2_400x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/c/c/0/cc014d38a73b249896400b7a15723d3aa954b65e.jpeg)
>
> https://linux.do#p-24987401-h-5第二次见面，还是有点紧张的
>
> 后来隔了两天，我又找她聊了几句。
>
> 聊的都是咖啡，偶尔聊聊工作。
>
> 知道她也在附近上班，平时工作挺忙的。
>
> 我就问她，周末有没有时间，上次说的那家咖啡店要不要去试试。
>
> 她说周六下午可以。
>
> 我就把位置和时间发给她，她说好。
>
> 说实话，约出来的时候我还是挺开心的。
>
> 毕竟我本来只是想买个咖啡机，结果现在还要请卖家喝咖啡。（这机器买得确实值）
>
> 周六我提前到了十几分钟。
>
> 特意挑了个靠窗的位置，光线比较好。
>
> 因为第一次见面是晚上，电梯里灯光也不太好，虽然觉得她好看，但是没看得特别清楚。
>
> 这次她穿了一件浅色上衣，头发披着，和第一次见面不太一样。
>
> 走过来的时候我第一眼就认出来了。
>
> 确实挺好看的，不是那种很夸张的漂亮，就是干干净净，特别舒服的感觉。
>
> 她看到我就笑了，说，你今天不会又有什么东西要我教吧。
>
> 我说，没有，今天主要来验收一下老师的教学成果。
>
> 她说，你还装。
>
> 然后我们两个都笑了。
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/d/2/a/d2a3e8eeed48783c2701795ada0e0280d0eed133_2_400x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/d/2/a/d2a3e8eeed48783c2701795ada0e0280d0eed133.jpeg)
>
> https://linux.do#p-24987401-h-6聊天的时候，发现她比想象中有意思
>
> 点咖啡的时候，她点了一杯热拿铁，我点了一杯冰美式。
>
> 她问我，你怎么不喝拿铁。
>
> 我说，天天喝奶咖也会腻，今天换个口味。
>
> 她说，那你昨天还问我哪家奶咖好喝。
>
> 我愣了一下。
>
> 这姑娘记性还挺好。
>
> 我说，因为我不是来研究咖啡的。
>
> 她问，那你来研究什么。
>
> 我说，研究一下为什么一个卖咖啡机的人，能把买家教得这么认真。
>
> 她笑了，说，你是不是平时就这么会说话。
>
> 我说，真没有，主要看跟谁说。

### [解决T3 Code开代理后 T3 Connect 报 cloudflared 连不上的问题（附多设备注意事项）](https://linux.do/t/topic/3206018)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-19 13:52 UTC · zh-CN · by pinguuu

> 最近折腾 T3 Code 想搞一下电脑和手机互通，开 T3 Connect 的时候电脑端一直卡在这个报错：
>
> ```
> T3 Connect is on, but other devices cannot reach this environment.
>
> cloudflared has not connected to Cloudflare yet. Fix: Wait a minute. If it stays, check the network and the server log.
>
> ```
>
> 等了半天也没自动好。看了一眼 ~/.t3/userdata/logs/relay-client.ndjson 日志，发现 cloudflared 一直在连 198.18.0.x:7844——破案了，这是 Clash Verge 的 TUN + Fake-IP 把 Cloudflare 隧道域名解析成了假 IP 并截走了流量，导致 QUIC/TLS 握手一直失败。
>
> 不想关代理也不想影响 T3 Code 正常跑，直接给当前订阅加直连和 Fake-IP 白名单就行，亲测不用重启 T3 Code，等一两分钟就通了。
>
> ---
>
> https://linux.do#p-24987010-clash-verge-1解决办法（Clash Verge）
>
> 前提：右上角保持在 「规则」 模式，不要切「全局」。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24987010-h-1-21. 给隧道域名加前置直连规则
>
> 左侧点 「订阅」 → 右键你正在用的那张订阅卡片 → 「编辑规则」，添加下面 3 条规则：
>
> 类型选 匹配域名后缀（DOMAIN-SUFFIX）
>
> 策略选 直接连接（DIRECT）
>
> 域名依次填：
>
> argotunnel.com
>
> cfargotunnel.com
>
> t3coderelay.com
>
> 注意点 「添加前置规则」，不要点成「添加后置规则」（后置排在 MATCH,PROXY 后面不生效）。加完点保存。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24987010-h-2-fake-ip-32. 把这几个域名排除出 Fake-IP
>
> 光加直连规则还不够，地址还是会被解析成 198.18.*。
>
> 还是右键这张订阅卡片 → 「扩展覆写配置」，把下面这段贴进去保存：
>
> ```
> dns:
>   fake-ip-filter:
>     - "*.lan"
>     - "*.local"
>     - "*.arpa"
>     - "time.*.com"
>     - "ntp.*.com"
>     - "+.market.xiaomi.com"
>     - "localhost.ptlogin2.qq.com"
>     - "*.msftncsi.com"
>     - "www.msftconnecttest.com"
>     - "+.argotunnel.com"
>     - "+.cfargotunnel.com"
>     - "+.t3coderelay.com"
> ```
>
> 别去改「设置 → Clash 设置 → DNS 覆写」，那个会影响整份订阅的 DNS，容易把节点搞挂。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24987010-h-4验证
>
> 保存后等一两分钟，去 Clash Verge 的「连接」里看，发往 7844 端口的目标 IP 从 198.18.* 变成 198.41.* 就说明通了，T3 Code 里的警告也会自己消掉。
>
> (注：如果本地网络直连 Cloudflare 7844 本身被阻断，那就把上面三条规则的策略从 DIRECT 改成你支持 UDP/TCP 转发的稳定节点，Fake-IP 过滤依然保留。)
>
> ---
>
> https://linux.do#p-24987010-h-5多设备互通注意事项
>
> 顺手整理几个实际用起来容易踩的坑：
>
> 电脑端：
>
> Clash 保持 「规则」 模式，切到「全局」前置规则会失效；换新订阅卡片时规则不会自动带过去，得重新加一遍。
>
> 电脑得开机且 T3 Code 不能把最后一个窗口关掉（关掉就停本地服务了），不想留窗口可以用 t3 up 放后台跑。
>
> 电脑休眠唤醒后隧道重连比较慢，一直连不上就彻底退出 T3 Code 重开一次。
>
> Mac 上有 Tailscale 的话别开出口节点（Exit Node），会把隧道流量拐走。
>
> 手机端：
>
> 手机不用连电脑上的 Clash，各自走各自的网络去连 Cloudflare 中转。手机端能直连就别开代理；打不开再开手机自己的代理（能正常访问 *.t3coderelay.com 的 HTTPS 就行，不用放行 7844）。
>
> 电脑和手机的系统时间都开「自动设置」，时间对不上会导致认证被拒。
>
> 开了「新设备需要批准」的话，手机端会出短码，去电脑 Settings → Sharing & access 核对放行。
>
> 在同一 Wi-Fi 或同一 Tailscale 网络下也可以直接走局域网/Tailscale（Settings → Sharing & access 里打开 Network access，手机代理记得放行内网和 100.64.0.0/10）。

### [Workbuddy 对于企业定制软件交付领域的冲击，可能比我们想象的都要大](https://linux.do/t/topic/3205993)

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-19 13:49 UTC · zh-CN · by DouglasDong

> 近期刚被拉进内部 Agent Harness 底座的项目做技术负责人，这几天听下来产品经理总结前场交付的困境和问题，感觉 Workbuddy 及其他 AI 办公类产品，对整个企业定制软件领域的冲击可能一直被过分低估了。
>
> 作为一个主攻领域为 2G 端，面向央国企交付的部门，从今年 7 月开始，前场遇到的销售难题如下（凭记忆复述）：
>
> Workbuddy 正在做大量的面向企业一号位、一把手的一对一试用账号体验，目前虽然没有正式接入企业内部办公网，但已经在领导层建立起了初步的用户心智
>
> 目前，对于央国企及政府机关单位，均在做一定程度上的 Agent Harness 底座自建及采购
>
> 央国企的标书及评标，也在由过去的采购单一软件，转向采购统一的 Agent Harness 平台 + 定制插件 / 连接器的形式
>
> 部门内部去年销售成绩不错的基于 LLM 深度定制的单点软件（如 PPT 生成或会议纪要方面），今年开始普遍在投标阶段一轮游，很难进入到第二阶段，即便有进入到第二阶段的情况，也会被要求提供对应的插件 / 连接器进行软件接入
>
> 客户对部门目前提供的单点软件产品，普遍会顾虑 LLM 发展速度偏快，一旦采购交付后，第二年很快会过时
>
> 所以，部门内部目前正在紧急立项做 Agent Harness 底座。因为上层判断，一旦今年不能拿出对应的底座产品，明年开始，部门整体的定制交付销售都会非常困难，最终会彻底沦为 Workbuddy 的插件定制商

>
> 今年 8 月，我们熟知的、饱受爱戴的明星科学家 JD 从 Google 离职。DH 则退出 DM 管理一线，放手 Gemini，专心研究生物医药。
>
> 无名小卒 Koray Kavukcuoglu 代替了 DH。
>
> 这位无名小卒，在 DQN，wavenet，alphago，alpha star 等等 AI 史上的重要事件中都有极其重大的贡献。是 A3C 的主要作者。alphafold 初代的共同作者之一。Google 天气预报项目重要贡献者。开创性成就数不胜数。
>
> Koray 很可能能算得上这个世界上最具能力的一群工程师之一。DH 当年的诸多大项目，背后的工程落地就是他在干。
>
> ---
>
> 在 koray 之下，优秀的年轻人想必不会太少。

### [用《西游记》理解 agent](https://linux.do/t/topic/3205774)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-19 13:17 UTC · zh-CN · by flingjie

> [![图片](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/c/0/4/c04e44871fb4215649cafcce10312ee8c3bf8915_2_333x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/c/0/4/c04e44871fb4215649cafcce10312ee8c3bf8915.jpeg)
>
> 把 agent 看做孙悟空，很聪明，本事很多，七十二变，还有厉害工具，金箍棒和筋斗云，但也会「心猿意马」：跑偏、绕圈、急着交差。作为唐僧，要控制孙悟空，就要学会方法。不能像如来那样，用五行山压着，就不能发挥孙悟空的能力，而需要运用合适的方法进行控制，只在关键时刻用紧箍咒进行控制。合适的方法包括：
>
> Harness engineering。 给悟空定好目标，提供提供条件和工具，规定权限职责，可以打妖怪，不能伤害百姓。
>
> Loop engineering， 不断打怪，打错了惩罚，做对了奖励，让他自我迭代，自我成长。
>
> Graph engineering，控制取经路线，是去西方，不要走到东方去了。

> Knowvori 是一个Agent skill，让 AI 把你的学习需求，做成一节能动手操作的网页课，比较适合想学习新知识，或者是准备面试的人群。

> 贴个logo:

> [![logo](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/b/0/3/b038b89a30e71dffb6e1cd7c6257ac72329b2ddd_2_500x500.webp)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/b/0/3/b038b89a30e71dffb6e1cd7c6257ac72329b2ddd.webp)
>
> 它是什么：
>
> 一个给 Agent 用的教学 Skill。装到支持 Skill 的 AI 工具里，你说想学什么、现在什么基础、学完想做到什么，然后它就开始设计课程，并生成可交互的有趣的网页，同时支持npx skills add直接安装。

> 它能干什么：
>
> 生成文件简洁直观：最终的产物是一个单文件 HTML 课程

> 效果直观：界面中有可以交互的部分，不限于可拖滑块、转 3D、点按钮的演示

>
> 情景检验：用新情境检验，避免“看懂了但不会用”
>
> 本地优先：离线、手机、深色模式都能用

### [【开源】Rust + GPUI 的 SSH 客户端这么多，为什么还要选 OxideTerm？（1.9K Star / v2.4.0）](https://linux.do/t/topic/3205705)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-19 13:06 UTC · zh-CN · by soleilune

> 开源推广申明 [（点击了解更多详细信息）](https://linux.do/t/topic/3205705/1)
> 大家好，我是[OxideTerm](https://github.com/AnalyseDeCircuit/oxideterm)的作者。
>
> 来简单介绍下OxideTerm吧，这是一个免费开源的原生 SSH 客户端，更是一个远程服务器工作区。Win、MacOS、Linux三端通吃。你能想到的SSH客户端基础功能基本这里都有： SSH、Mosh、Telnet、串口、BLE、RDP、VNC、SFTP、本地终端、远程文本编辑、端口转发、主机监控，AI辅助、MCP。基于Rust+GPUI的一切性能和内存优势，那更不必多说。现在在Github上大概1.9K star。
>
> 不过我想，各位佬友们看到这里肯定会问一个问题：诶，可是现在SSH客户端都泛滥了啊，Rust+GPUI的更是不在少数，虽然你的功能很全面，但是我凭什么来用你的软件？你有什么优势？解决了我什么痛点？
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/4/5/6/45689c179c213b1a2d5de0a71788f914b6cf4805_2_517x302.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/4/5/6/45689c179c213b1a2d5de0a71788f914b6cf4805.png)
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/8/2/5/8259118907eb7017bff031f359685eb00fe5179f_2_517x258.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/8/2/5/8259118907eb7017bff031f359685eb00fe5179f.jpeg)
>
> （如图是刚切换到GPUI那段时间的空载内存情况）
>
> https://linux.do#p-24985357-rust-gpui-oxideterm-2Rust + GPUI 客户端这么多了，为什么还要选 OxideTerm？
>
> OxideTerm 项目起步挺早（今年1月），早期上过阮一峰周刊，功能也比较全面了，不过主包比较懒，没怎么在L站做过宣传。而现在时代变了，用 Rust + GPUI 和 Go Native 写的 SSH 客户端不少，好几个也在长期认真维护，各有各的长处。
>
> 现在的及格线大家都能轻松达到——轻快，省内存，能连上。基于这样的情况，其实我们更想解决的是连上以后的痛点：能否让佬友们开箱即用，降低迁移阻力？每天反复做的那些琐碎操作，能不能像老牌工具那样顺手？能不能减少无端操作，不要用着用着，气的就想一拳砸穿电脑屏幕？外观是否满足人最基本的审美要求？
>
> 所以，思路很简单：别人已经做的很顺手的地方直接学过来，别人还没做顺手的地方或者传统软件的痛点我们自己补上。
>
> [![截屏2026-11-16 22.55.24](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/3/2/5/325c70ec08f2b69237245aa799acdc85a40d6f86_2_690x192.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/3/2/5/325c70ec08f2b69237245aa799acdc85a40d6f86.png)
>
> https://linux.do#p-24985357-h-3博采众长之外，一些小绝活
>
> 当然，光博采众长是不够的，有差异才有辨识度。这里列出我觉得的一些差异点，部分功能是各位contributor PR的，也很感谢他们。原谅作者列举不周，佬友也可以自行探索，发现一些神秘小巧思。
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/c/7/e/c7e0ebf31f839d4b5764d85c058fc8b2a229b83c_2_690x125.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/c/7/e/c7e0ebf31f839d4b5764d85c058fc8b2a229b83c.png)
>
> ![container-file-edit-small](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/7/8/2/782c56a1a6498a75a95ab1ead99681925d498bca.gif)
>
> https://linux.do#p-24985357-h-4写在最后
>
> 所以我们的答案是各家的好用之处都有了，再加上几处别人还没顾上的省心的点。
>
> 重剑无锋，大巧不工。我认为或许对于一个工具来说，平时没什么存在感但足够可靠，偶尔抬眼看下 UI 也挺顺眼，用的舒心就很好了。相比于短时爆发，我更希望 OxideTerm 能一路走下去，陪大家用得更久一点。
>
> 目前我一直都在更新，也十分欢迎佬友们下载体验。平时用着哪里别扭或者缺了什么顺手的功能，提 Issue、PR 就行，觉得还算顺手也求个 Star。另外 iOS / Android 移动端也快推出了（不过这算另一个项目了），到时候就是全平台五端云同步，相信大家会喜欢。
>
> GitHub：[GitHub - AnalyseDeCircuit/oxideterm: Fast, native Rust + GPUI workspace for local and SSH with MCP tools—no WebView, no telemetry, open source. · GitHub](https://github.com/AnalyseDeCircuit/oxideterm)
>
> 下载：[Release OxideTerm Native 2.4.0 · AnalyseDeCircuit/oxideterm · GitHub](https://github.com/AnalyseDeCircuit/oxideterm/releases/latest)
>
> 官网：https://oxideterm.app/
>
> 帖子有点长了，其他截图我都放在下面折叠了，佬友们可以打开看，相信各位会喜欢我们的UI的。
>
> 所有的截图 [（点击了解更多详细信息）](https://linux.do/t/topic/3205705/1)

>
> 题图为 AI 生成
>
> [![OMP Studio](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/7/9/1/7918d17a12125249a90a87f6d0c966104bb9a2fb.svg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/7/9/1/7918d17a12125249a90a87f6d0c966104bb9a2fb.svg)
>
> OMP Studio
>
> 各位佬好，来推一下自己写了三个多月的东西
>
> 仓库： [GitHub - the-snowpear/omp-studio · GitHub](https://github.com/the-snowpear/omp-studio)
>
> https://linux.do#p-24985240-h-1这是什么
>
> [oh-my-pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi)（下面简称 omp）是一个跑在终端里的 coding agent，基于 Pi 的一个超级功能大杂烩的cli工具。OMP Studio 是我给它做的桌面端，Windows / macOS / Linux 三平台支持。
>
> 我写的这个桌面端融入了很少有agent使用的全局窗口化设计，并开放了omp的绝大多数功能，包括通过acp或者其他方式没有开放出来的。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24985240-h-2为什么要做
>
> 有一段时间，我的我平时编程主力就是 omp，CLI 本身挺好用，但同时开三四个会话，再加上子 agent、审批、看 diff、开浏览器查东西，终端标签多到自己都找不着。同时，当时网上综合搜索后，并没有找到一个功能完善且ui完善的gui工具。
>
> 我在 runtime 里加了一层类型化的 bridge，界面直接调 runtime 的能力。代价是自己维护一份对上游的补丁，不能直接使用上游的原生ompcli
>
> 前段时间，我发布了0.2.0版本，加入了目前没有在主流agent看到的全功能窗口化设计，加入了我自己的很多ui和交互的小巧思。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24985240-h-3基本概览
>
> 下面是真实界面录屏，可以展示应用的基本的交互逻辑
>
> ![拖动对话变成浮窗并吸附分屏](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/0/9/e/09eef56b03187902eab0b9b5d83ce8fb5f6b5b31.webp)
>
> 拖动对话变成浮窗并吸附分屏
>
> 0.2.0 把整个工作台推倒重做了一遍，现在对话和工具都是窗口：
>
> 侧栏里的会话直接拖出来就是一个浮窗，拖到边缘或角落会自动吸附分屏，类似 Windows 的窗口贴靠
>
> 悬停最大化按钮会弹出布局模板，左右各半、三列、四宫格这些
>
> Git、文件、终端、浏览器、日志这些工具可以停在左栏、右栏、底栏、对话旁边，或者干脆浮着
>
> 浮窗还能钉成独立的系统窗口，拖到副屏上
>
> 窗口挪来挪去不会重建对话，草稿、滚动位置、终端状态都还在
>
> 三窗口布局
>
> [![三窗口布局](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/0/5/c/05cddc23fd8b870868bbc415551d481e5ce1d048_2_690x431.webp)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/0/5/c/05cddc23fd8b870868bbc415551d481e5ce1d048.webp)
>
> 下面这张停靠位置示意图为 AI 生成
>
> [![五种停靠位置示意](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/8/9/c/89c9693c38f775ca32f8f27cfc3aed87720901ca.svg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/8/9/c/89c9693c38f775ca32f8f27cfc3aed87720901ca.svg)
>
> 五种停靠位置示意
>
> https://linux.do#p-24985240-h-4其他功能
>
> Agent Hub：主会话和所有子 agent 的状态、请求数、token、花费放在一页看
>
> 模型配置：Anthropic、OpenAI、OpenRouter、本地 LM Studio 都在一页管，类似老版ccswitch，可以给 @plan、@task 这些角色单独指定模型和思考强度
>
> Time Travel：按回合存工作区快照，可以只回滚代码、只回滚对话，或者一起回滚（默认是关的）
>
> 内置浏览器：多标签，人和 agent 可以互相交接控制
>
> 能力中心：Skills、MCP、Plugins、Slash Commands 在一页开关
>
> 还有语音输入、文件预览（PDF / Excel / 图片等）、SSH 远程工作区（这个还是开发预览）

### [给佬们分享一下Tarobird的Codex、Claude Code 、DSH 、AGY、KIMI互相调度功能](https://linux.do/t/topic/3205689)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-19 13:04 UTC · zh-CN · by 奥森木

> Tarobird功能蛮多的，Codex、Claude Code 、DSH 、AGY、KIMI互相调度功能是其中之一，也是我最常用的功能。
>
> 我举个例子：
>
> 我要开个issue，但我想让codex和Claude一起做，于是我输入：
>
> “我想开个issue，是关于显示我们各个模型还剩多少使用额度的，你和opus5.5商量一下，这个issue怎么写，并提出”
>
> [![截屏2026-11-19 下午8.41.17](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/d/9/b/d9b5eff813ea2855a46b28f1626c32b25e4226c3_2_575x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/d/9/b/d9b5eff813ea2855a46b28f1626c32b25e4226c3.jpeg)
>
> 之后codex就会调用opus，并讨论
>
> [![截屏2026-11-19 下午8.44.13](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/b/5/4/b540bad83c48b8582f16503424ed62ccdc2700bc_2_575x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/b/5/4/b540bad83c48b8582f16503424ed62ccdc2700bc.jpeg)
>
> 这时候可以看到codex新调用了一个claude的对话，他们会进行多轮讨论
>
> [![截屏2026-11-19 下午8.47.50](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/9/c/7/9c7e06e0a85842a136e68feeed662d0acfd39160_2_577x500.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/9/c/7/9c7e06e0a85842a136e68feeed662d0acfd39160.png)
>
> codex会实时接收claude的反馈
>
> [![截屏2026-11-19 下午8.52.03](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/7/6/b/76b0c20a3ceab38f1a588f192300857f681784d4_2_576x500.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/7/6/b/76b0c20a3ceab38f1a588f192300857f681784d4.png)
>
> 最终claude给出结果
>
> [![截屏2026-11-19 下午8.54.18](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/0/a/0/0a0ecfa2db8e0ccc1ddcd47c0545f3daa1cd8b12_2_578x500.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/0/a/0/0a0ecfa2db8e0ccc1ddcd47c0545f3daa1cd8b12.png)
>
> 然后codex选择他的采纳部分
>
> [![截屏2026-11-19 下午8.55.39](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/3/9/0/390e461290d8a3cbb6d9e68199d5d17f3f89867c_2_574x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/3/9/0/390e461290d8a3cbb6d9e68199d5d17f3f89867c.jpeg)
>
> 这是最后的issue
>
> [![截屏2026-11-19 下午8.56.10](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/9/a/1/9a1d0fae07521f1a114a7c85a69243b7eea55345_2_389x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/9/a/1/9a1d0fae07521f1a114a7c85a69243b7eea55345.jpeg)
>
> 其实不光是issue，包括编程我会大量的用多bot相互调度，因为单一模型的思考确实有限。图里是指举了codex和claude的例子，其他模型间也可以。
>
> Tarobird是我开源的IM，具体见[TaroBird：一个给 AI Agent 用的 IM，把电脑上的 Codex、Claude Code、DeepSeek 等 CLI 变成随身助手，手机远程同步派活和审批，Win / Mac / iOS / 安卓多端支持 - #9，来自 cloveric](https://linux.do/t/topic/3195209/9)
